name: STAYUP Saitama Omiya
card: Window seats with a view of Mt Fuji, ten minutes from the West Exit of Omiya Station
title: STAYUP Saitama Omiya — a shared office with a café space, ten minutes from Omiya Station
lead: STAYUP Saitama Omiya, a coworking space and shared office, is on the 8th floor of the OS Building in Sakuragicho 4-chome, about a ten-minute walk from the West Exit of Omiya Station. STAYUP's fourth site, its open, airy space includes sit-stand desks, window seats, sofa seats, partitioned desks and focus booths. On clear days, you can see Mt Fuji from the window seats. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Omiya Station West Exit, about 10 min walk (JR, Tobu Noda Line, New Shuttle)
Staffed weekdays 9:00–18:00 except holidays (unstaffed at other times)
concept: Choose your seat to suit how you work
STAYUP Saitama Omiya is STAYUP's fourth site. Its open workspace has ergonomic chairs and quality tables.
Besides the open space, there are sit-stand desks, window seats, sofa seats screened from view and desks enclosed by side panels, so you can choose a seat to suit your work style.
steps: The open space is furnished with high-performance chairs. Drop-in comes in three tiers — ¥880, ¥1,650 and ¥2,750 — from one hour to a full day.
On clear days, Mt Fuji is visible from the window seats.
Seats to suit your work style
Sofas for meetings, booths for web sales calls
Sofa seats screened from view are used for meetings and lunch.
Focus booths work for concentrated work, online meetings and web sales calls.
About 30 drinks, and rooms for 6 and 8
The café space has about 30 kinds of free drinks, plus vending machines and light snacks.
Meeting rooms cost ¥2,200 an hour for 6 people and ¥2,750 for 8, with large monitors and whiteboards. Monthly members get ¥550 an hour off.

word.title: What is a sit-stand desk?
body: A desk whose top can be raised and lowered, so you can work sitting or standing.
STAYUP Saitama Omiya offers sit-stand desks as one of its seat types.

credits: STAYUP (listed in the official website footer as a Radix Group site)

name: PORT2401 (Shinagawa City Nishi-Oi Startup Support Center)
card: A Shinagawa City base for entrepreneurs, one minute from Nishi-Oi Station
title: PORT2401 (Shinagawa City Nishi-Oi Startup Support Center) — Shinagawa City's start-up support coworking, one minute from Nishi-Oi Station
lead: PORT2401, the Shinagawa City Nishi-Oi Startup Support Center, is on the 2nd floor of J Tower Nishi-Oi East Tower, a one-minute walk from Nishi-Oi Station on the JR Yokosuka Line. For entrepreneurs from before founding to under three years in business, it offers a coworking space, multipurpose space, meeting rooms, a kitchen and more. Drop-in costs ¥2,000 a day for general users. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: PORT2401 (Shinagawa City Nishi-Oi Startup Support Center)
JR Yokosuka Line Nishi-Oi Station, 1 min walk
concept: Your start-up voyage begins here
PORT2401 is a Shinagawa City facility that supports entrepreneurs — from before founding to under three years in business — from launch to growth.
The official website says it aims to create an environment where you can get advice, connect, try things out and learn. It is run by Noot Ltd. on commission from Shinagawa City.
steps: The coworking space is for focused work. The official website describes it as surrounded by plants and designed to help you concentrate.
Monthly membership is ¥8,000 (general) or ¥5,000 (students). Drop-in is ¥2,000 a day (general) or ¥1,300 (students).
The multipurpose space is normally used for networking and work, and can be rented as an event venue at ¥2,000 per hour for private use.
Meeting rooms are bookable, with rooms for 6 and 8 that can be combined for more than ten people, at ¥300 per hour.
The kitchen space is free to use for coffee breaks and lunch.
A place to try things, and a place to meet
In the pop-up space, members can sell their products or display information about their services.
The café space is used for quick meetings between members and outside guests, and as a waiting area for visitors. A community manager is stationed at reception.

word.title: What is a startup support center?
body: A facility set up by a local government or similar body for people thinking of starting a business or who have just started one. Besides workspace, it offers advice and networking.
PORT2401 is run by Shinagawa City, and puts spaces for trying things out and learning on the same floor as its coworking.

name: Kaikokan (TUAT West Tokyo International Innovation Co-creation Hub)
card: A co-creation hub open to the community, on TUAT's Fuchu campus
title: Kaikokan (TUAT West Tokyo International Innovation Co-creation Hub) — a co-creation hub on the Fuchu campus of Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology
lead: Take a bus from Fuchu Station on the Keio Line or Kokubunji Station on the JR Chuo Line to “Harumicho (Tokyo Noko Daigaku-mae)”. On the Fuchu campus of Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology (TUAT) stands Kaikokan, the West Tokyo International Innovation Co-creation Hub. The ground-floor cafeteria and the 2nd-floor Three-University Co-creation Space are open to anyone, and the 2nd floor also has members-only coworking and private offices. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Kaikokan (TUAT West Tokyo International Innovation Co-creation Hub)
Bus from Keio Line Fuchu Station or JR Chuo Line Kokubunji Station to “Harumicho (Tokyo Noko Daigaku-mae)” / JR Musashino Line Kita-Fuchu Station, about 12 min walk
Cafeteria & Three-University Co-creation Space 8:00–21:00 / shared office (members only) 8:00–23:00
Shared office: individual ¥22,000/month, corporate (4 people) ¥60,500/month (incl. tax, paid half-yearly in advance)
concept: Where the region meets the world, woven by university knowledge
Kaikokan is a co-creation hub that Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology set up on its Fuchu campus. Its main themes are agriculture, food and energy.

The ground floor has a cafeteria, a MUJI shop, an agriculture-and-food restaurant and an event space; the 2nd floor is the incubation space; and the 3rd floor has a lounge, an outdoor terrace and a solar-sharing demonstration area.
steps: A 2nd-floor learning space open to all

The 2nd-floor Three-University Co-creation Space is designed for active learning. It is open to everyone, including students of TUAT, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Electro-Communications.
It is available from 8:00 to 21:00, and may close for events.
A ground-floor space where anyone can sit
The ground-floor cafeteria is a relaxed space open to all. You can eat food bought in the building, or bring your own.
MUJI and the agriculture-and-food restaurant are on the same floor.
The 2nd-floor shared office has 96 coworking seats, four private offices, meeting rooms and a test kitchen, available 8:00–23:00.

Individual membership is ¥22,000 a month and corporate membership ¥60,500 a month (four people). You apply after a tour and interview, and screening usually takes about a month. Meeting rooms are free for up to 30 hours a month.

word.title: What is solar sharing?
body: Installing solar panels above farmland to generate electricity while still growing crops, also called agrivoltaics.
At Kaikokan, solar sharing on the 3rd floor serves as a demonstration and research area for urban agriculture.

credits: Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology (naming rights: Musashi Engineering, Inc.)

name: AGORA KGU KANNAI
card: Coworking inside a university campus, two minutes from Kannai Station
title: AGORA KGU KANNAI — coworking on the Kanto Gakuin University Kannai campus
lead: AGORA KGU KANNAI, a coworking space and shared office, is on the 4th floor of Kanto Gakuin University's Yokohama-Kannai campus, a two-minute walk from Kannai Station. It has a free space, single and double private rooms, meeting rooms and a web-meeting room. Non-members can drop in on weekdays from 10:00 to 17:00. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Kanto Gakuin University Yokohama-Kannai campus, 4th floor
From ¥500/hour, ¥1,500/day (incl. tax; weekdays 10:00–17:00; no registration or booking needed)
concept: A workplace on the 4th floor of a university campus
AGORA KGU KANNAI is a coworking space and shared office on the 4th floor of Kanto Gakuin University's Yokohama-Kannai campus, run by AGORA Inc.
Services include company registration, start-up support, mail handling, a copier, lockers and meeting rooms.
steps: Non-members can drop into the free space on weekdays from 10:00 to 17:00, from ¥500 an hour or ¥1,500 a day (incl. tax).
Monthly memberships are Full-time (8:00–22:00) and Night & Holiday (weekdays 18:00–22:00, weekends and holidays 8:00–22:00).

Single rooms come in corridor-side and window-side types; double rooms are fully private with their own air conditioning. Both are furnished, allow company registration and include up to 15 hours of free meeting-room use a month.
Meeting rooms and a web-meeting room
Meeting rooms are for members only, at ¥1,000 an hour. There is also a web-meeting room, a business meeting area and a drinks booth.
Options include company registration (¥5,000/month), a mailbox (¥5,000/month) and a locker (¥2,000/month).

word.title: What is a Night & Holiday plan?
body: A monthly plan for weekday evenings plus weekends and holidays, often aimed at office workers preparing a side business or start-up.
At AGORA KGU KANNAI, it lets you use the free space on weekdays 18:00–22:00 and on weekends and holidays 8:00–22:00.

credits: © AGORA KGU KANNAI (official website: top page)
AGORA KGU KANNAI official website: top page

name: AGORA Hon-atsugi
card: Coworking on the 6th floor of a station building, directly linked to Hon-Atsugi Station
title: AGORA Hon-atsugi — coworking inside Mylord, directly linked to Hon-Atsugi Station
lead: AGORA Hon-atsugi is a coworking space on the 6th floor of Hon-Atsugi Mylord 1, the station building directly linked to Hon-Atsugi Station on the Odakyu Odawara Line. It has a free space, single private rooms and single booths, with drop-in available on weekdays from 10:00 to 17:00. It is also a base for Kanagawa Prefecture's HATSU entrepreneur support programme. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Directly linked to Odakyu Odawara Line Hon-Atsugi Station (turn left from the North Exit to Mylord 1, 6F)
concept: A start-up base inside a station building
AGORA Hon-atsugi is a coworking space run by AGORA Inc. Its official website says it is a base for Kanagawa Prefecture's HATSU entrepreneur support programme, providing start-up support.
It is on the 6th floor of a shopping building directly linked to Hon-Atsugi Station; follow the signs from the North Exit.
steps: The free space is open to drop-ins on weekdays from 10:00 to 17:00, at ¥500 an hour, ¥1,000 for three hours or ¥1,500 a day (incl. tax).
Monthly membership is ¥14,000, and the Night & Holiday plan (weekdays 17:00–22:00 plus weekends and holidays) is ¥8,900.
Single rooms and single booths are also available for drop-in, at ¥750 an hour, ¥1,250 for three hours or ¥1,750 a day.
Monthly rates are ¥29,800 for a single room and ¥24,000 for a single booth.
Options include company registration (¥5,000/month), an online school with start-up consultations (¥2,980/month), a mailbox (¥5,000/month) and a locker (¥2,000/month).

word.title: What does “directly linked to the station” mean?
body: You can walk from the station gates or concourse into the building without going outside.
AGORA Hon-atsugi is on the 6th floor of Hon-Atsugi Mylord 1, which is directly linked to Hon-Atsugi Station, so you can get there without stepping outside.

credits: AGORA Hon-atsugi official website: top page

name: Shinjuku Natural Hot Spring Thermae-Yu
card: Partitioned work seats in a 24-hour hot spring in Shinjuku
title: Shinjuku Natural Hot Spring Thermae-Yu — coworking and lounges in a Kabukicho hot spring
lead: Shinjuku Natural Hot Spring Thermae-Yu, in Kabukicho 1-chome, is a 24-hour bathhouse about a two-minute walk from Exit E1 of Shinjuku-sanchome Station on the Tokyo Metro and Toei Shinjuku Line. On the ground floor, inside the locker-room area, is a coworking space with individually partitioned seats, and a Relax & Coworking Lounge opened on the basement floor in July 2025. Every seat has power, and free Wi-Fi is available. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 1F coworking space / B1F Relax & Coworking Lounge
Tokyo Metro Marunouchi & Fukutoshin lines and Toei Shinjuku Line Shinjuku-sanchome Station Exit E1, about 2 min walk / JR Shinjuku Station East Exit, about 9 min
Open 24 hours, every day of the year
concept: Sauna and work, under one roof
Thermae-Yu describes its ground-floor coworking space as making possible “the luxurious lifestyle of sauna × workation”.
It suggests refreshing yourself in the baths, then working or reading in a gentle focus mode. There are several lounges for resting too.
steps: The ground-floor coworking space is set up separately for men and women inside the locker-room area.
Each desk is partitioned, every seat has USB and power outlets, and free Wi-Fi is available.
The Relax & Coworking Lounge, opened July 2025
The basement Relax & Coworking Lounge opened on 1 July 2025 and is free to use.
There are 24 relaxation beds and 11 coworking seats, all with power outlets.
A women-only lounge and a waiting lounge
The 3rd-floor Venus Lounge is a space where women can relax on their own with peace of mind, at no extra charge. Every seat has a TV and USB and power outlets, with free Wi-Fi.
On the second basement level there is a double-height relaxation lounge, and on the ground floor a lounge room (waiting room).

word.title: What is a workation?
body: A blend of “work” and “vacation”: working while travelling or taking a break somewhere restful.
Thermae-Yu calls using the sauna and coworking under one roof “sauna × workation”.

credits: Shinjuku Natural Hot Spring Thermae-Yu official website: “Top”, “Other facilities”

name: Sauna & Hotel Karumaru Ikebukuro
card: Work desks in a sauna and hotel, 30 seconds from Ikebukuro Station
title: Sauna & Hotel Karumaru Ikebukuro — coworking in a sauna's rest area, 30 seconds from the West Exit of Ikebukuro Station
lead: Sauna & Hotel Karumaru Ikebukuro, in Ikebukuro 2-chome, is a 30-second walk from Exit C6 on the west side of Ikebukuro Station. A facility for saunas and overnight stays, it has a coworking space — desks free to use for work — inside its rest area. There are also recliners, capsule-style relaxation pods and a library of more than 10,000 manga and magazines. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Coworking space in the rest area
Ikebukuro Station West Exit C6, 30 sec walk
11:00–10:00 the next morning (baths until 9:00; open daily except specified days)
concept: A café-like workplace after the sauna
The official website describes the coworking space as a functional space where you can focus on work in a café-like atmosphere.
The rest area offers many kinds of space to choose from — recliners, relaxation pods, a library and coworking — so you can decide how to spend time after the sauna.
steps: The recliner space has purpose-designed recliners, with unlimited video on demand, reading lights and unlimited manga and magazines.
The relaxation pods are capsule-style rest spaces you enter between bookshelves, with mattresses so you can relax undisturbed. Neither can be reserved.
In the library space, you can read more than 10,000 manga and magazines freely at no charge, with new titles added regularly.
On the 7th floor, coffee from a house-roasting brand run by a well-known chef is on sale, made from rare Guatemalan beans roasted on site.
Guests are asked to keep quiet in the building, and some areas are designated no-call zones.

word.title: What is a sauna & hotel?
body: A bathhouse centred on saunas, combined with rooms or capsules for overnight stays.
Karumaru Ikebukuro offers overnight and day use, with a coworking space inside its rest area.

credits: Sauna & Hotel Karumaru Ikebukuro official website: “Top”, “Rest area”

name: Kasukabe Yumoto Onsen
card: Seats for reading and desk work in a Kasukabe hot spring
title: Kasukabe Yumoto Onsen — a space for desk work on the 2nd floor of a hot-spring facility
lead: Kasukabe Yumoto Onsen is a bathhouse in Shimo-Omasu-Shinden, Kasukabe. On the 2nd floor is a workspace for reading or a little desk work, alongside a rest zone and relaxation corner. It is open 10:00–23:00, and the restaurants inside can be used without paying the entry fee. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Adults: weekdays ¥1,650 / weekends & holidays ¥1,800 / night service ¥1,000 (entry after 20:00; incl. tax, with towel set; loungewear ¥200 extra)
concept: A little time at a desk after the bath
The official website presents the 2nd-floor workspace as a place for reading or a little desk work.
The same floor has a rest zone, a relaxation corner and chargers, so you can bathe, rest, do a bit of work and rest again.
steps: A 2nd floor for reading and desk work
The 2nd-floor workspace is for reading or a little desk work. Chargers are also available on this floor.
A 2nd-floor rest zone for after the bath
There is a rest zone on the same floor as the workspace.
Comfortable seats, and a ground-floor meeting point
The 2nd floor has a relaxation corner, and the ground floor a meeting zone.
The restaurants inside can be used without paying the entry fee.

word.title: What is the night service?
body: A discounted entry fee for people arriving late in the evening.
At Kasukabe Yumoto Onsen, adults who check in after 20:00 pay ¥1,000 (last entry 22:00).
